text:
maria: heads-up — noticed perf regression on canary yesterday; looks related to batching heuristics + kernel selection. want to run an offline trace-driven ensemble to tune batch formation, queue policy and token-budget targets before any prod changes.

jin: sounds good. which traces and what's the target?

maria: primary trace = traces/mar12-mix-420.json (mixed chat + completions, avg seq ~420, heavy tail up to ~3k). objective: reduce p99 gen latency by ~10% without increasing token cost >3%.

ryan: profiler snippet from canary: kernel oscillation around the 256/512 boundaries — scheduler flipping between fused-attn and fallback which spikes tail latency. snippet:
```
[profiler] seq=240 -> kernel=fused_kv_v2
[profiler] seq=260 -> kernel=fallback_attn
[profiler] seq=248 -> kernel=fused_kv_v2
# observed: latency spikes correlate with kernel_switch events
```

anika: kv cache hit-rate also down ~12% in canary; prefix normalization change caused more misses so more compute per token.

leo: proposing variants for offline sweep:
- baseline (current)
- A: token_budget_target 0.60 -> 0.75
- B: max_wait_ms 20 -> 12
- C: bias kernel selection toward fused when seq >= 280
- D: combo A+B+C
- E: clamp batch_max_tokens to 4096 to avoid kernel thrash on mixed sequences

maria: add variant F: D + slight prefix-normalize rollback to recover KV hits (we can simulate it separately).

jin: note adjusting token_budget up reduces batching depth in spikes — could increase cost. AB harness must capture p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost_per_1k, kv_hit_ratio, kernel_switch_rate and quality metrics.

replay-bot: queued sim: traces/mar12-mix-420.json -> variants [baseline,A,B,C,D,E,F]. command:
```
./tools/trace-sim run --trace traces/mar12-mix-420.json --variants baseline,A,B,C,D,E,F --out /tmp/sim-mar12-ensemble
```

ryan: also add a separate long-tail synthetic trace (traces/long-tail-2k.json) to stress >2k seqs; kernel bias can regress there. run separately and keep naming distinct.

bench-bot: queued sim jobs: sim-7623 (mar12 ensemble), sim-7624 (long-tail stress). ETA ~40-60m.

anika: when sims complete, run eval/ab/canary-metrics.yml harness against generated outputs (perplexity diff + checklist prompts) and produce A/B report.

leo: also add perf guard rails: fail early if kv_hit_ratio drops >6% or cost_per_1k increases >4% relative to baseline.

jin: sharing kernel bias config snippet for sims:
```
batching:
  token_budget_target: 0.60
  max_wait_ms: 20
kernel_selection:
  seq_bias_thresholds: [280]
  prefer_fused: true
```

maria: sounds good. action items:
- run sims + long-tail (leo)
- run A/B eval on sim outputs (anika)
- collect kernel_switch_rate and kv_hit_ratio aggregates (jin)
- stage 10% canary if D or F safe (ryan/maria)

bench-bot: sim-7623 complete — quick summary (baseline vs D):
- p99 baseline: 214ms -> D: 198ms (-7.5%)
- cost_per_1k baseline: $0.92 -> D: $0.95 (+3.3%)
- kv_hit_ratio baseline: 0.78 -> D: 0.73 (-6.4%)
- kernel_switch_rate baseline: 12/min -> D: 6/min

anika: D reduces latency but kv_hit_ratio drop is just over the 6% guard. run quality checks before approving.

jin: profiler overlays show kernel_switchs halved; fused kernel runs longer which smooths tail.

maria: proposal: try D' = D + small prefix-normalize rollback to recover KV hits. re-run only that variant.

leo: re-running D' (sim-7630).

bench-bot: sim-7630 complete. D' results:
- p99: 201ms (-6.1% vs baseline)
- cost_per_1k: $0.94 (+2.2%)
- kv_hit_ratio: 0.76 (-2.5%)
- quality checks: PASSED (no perplexity regression; prompt checklist OK)

maria: D' looks within our perf + cost + quality bounds. recommend staging canary with rollout: 10% traffic, 4h extended traces, auto-rollback if p99 > baseline + 10% OR kv_hit_ratio drop >5%. tagging @deploy-team for rollout PR.

ryan: creating canary rollout PR + infra ticket with extended trace hooks for kernel_switch and kv metrics.

anika: I'll run the eval harness during canary and monitor perplexity + checklist metrics live.

maria: thanks team. will close thread once canary is live and initial metrics are green. :white_check_mark:
